# Sector — Painkiller’s player review

- Original source: [Robin Hood](https://www.sector.sk/uzivatelrecenzia/156/robin-hood.htm)
- Author / publication: Painkiller; Sector.sk.
- Language / date: Slovak; 2005-05-20.
- Access: Full user review retrieved directly
- Checked: 2026-09-09
- Retrieved: 2026-09-09
- Archived copy: lookup failed (archive.org rate limit); not checked
- Format: header notes, original summary, then complete factual notes (user review on a commercial site, not transcribed)

Painkiller awards the game 9.5, emphasizing the relationship between sparing enemies and attracting recruits. The review describes combining character abilities, hiding incapacitated guards, seeking information from beggars, and responding to optional civilian requests. Once the named heroes are available, the author favors leaving ordinary recruits in camp to make supplies.

The limited variety of castle and forest maps is a criticism despite the enthusiastic overall assessment. This is a player’s account of tactics and reception, not an independently verified rules reference; incidental story details and numerical claims should be checked against the game.

## Detailed notes

Page facts: user review "Robin Hood" (platform PC) in Sector.sk's user reviews; "pridal Painkiller 20.5.2005 o 18:46"; score 9.5; signed "napísal Painkiller 20.5.2005"; no comment count shown; retrieved directly from sector.sk. Slovak user review on a commercial site, not transcribed.

Content, in order:

- Intro: the German team Spellbound, after the success of Desperados, decided to revive the Robin Hood legend.
- Section "O čo ide?" (what is it about): in 1190 Robin was away from England; his father, Lord of Locksley, died of old age (the reviewer notes Robin was really Robin of Locksley and took the name Hood as an outlaw); the Sheriff of Nottingham declared him dead and confiscated his property; King Richard I Lionheart sailed to the Holy Land; his younger brother Prince John (nicknamed Lackland, the reviewer explains, for losing the French possessions) took the throne and imposed high taxes; on his way back Richard was captured by Duke Leopold I, who set the ransom at 100,000 gold pieces; John refuses to pay, so Robin must collect the ransom.
- Section "Partia" (the band): first Stuteley joins (rescued from the gallows), with three villagers: a man with a pitchfork, one with an iron-shod staff, and an archer. The reviewer says there can be "even twenty" villagers in Sherwood depending on play style; mass battles with dozens of dead harm your reputation among villagers. "Robin was a thief, not a murderer"; best method is stun, tie up and hide, which wins many devoted fighters. Villagers are used in combat early; later, once the band is complete, they are left in Sherwood to make things: arrows for Robin, stones for Will Scarlet, nets for Stuteley, healing herbs for Lady Marion, etc. Later joiners: Will Scarlet ("Robin's nephew with brutal manners"), Lady Marion, strongman Little John, and the gluttonous Friar Tuck.
- Section "Ako to vlastne vyzerá?" (what it looks like): each character has their own traits and tactics. Robin: 100% archery, silent knockout with the fist, and throwing a purse of money, which distracts because stingy soldiers often fight over it, ending with one of four still conscious, though not all soldiers fall for it; he climbs and jumps anywhere possible and can search soldiers' pockets for money.
- Money: found in missions on soldiers or lying around, but most is earned in ambushes; money can also be spent. Beggars: clicking one automatically gives 50 "francs" (the reviewer's word; the price cannot be changed) for a tip shown as red messages on a part of the map, e.g. revealing soldiers on the map (soldiers and NPCs appear as shadows until you are close), where arrows are, or which soldier carries a lot of money.
- NPCs: good ones greet you, bad ones betray you, some ask for help as side tasks in missions or ambushes, e.g. curing a sick child (click Lady Marion and use healing herbs) or asking for food. Reward: four-leaf clovers, which give a dying member of Robin's band (not villagers) a chance to live.
- Structure: Sherwood is the hub from which ambushes and missions are organised. Missions are on five castles ("which is quite few"): Lincoln, Leicester, Derby, Nottingham, York. Ambushes are on three forest locations, usually robbing a tax collector protected by troops, or a convoy carrying gold; ambush areas are full of traps that help, though the reviewer regrets most must be activated by arrows.
- Technical: environment beautifully drawn, high-level graphics; music nice but you do not hear much of it; sounds good, as is the dubbing (the reviewer has the original with Czech dubbing). AI called very good: fighting three pikemen, when two are beaten the third runs to the nearest general and reports "Sir, I think the enemy is near"; the general orders two soldiers to search; the pikeman hides (e.g. in a church).
- Only two videos, at the start and end, "pitifully few".
- Verdict: a perfect strategy for a fairly long time; playability "amazing"; Commandos fans will find it a pleasant rest because it is not as demanding.
- Pluses: graphics, AI, length, music, tactical elements, dubbing. Minuses: few environments, few videos, no inventory.
- Closing tips: the most lives are spared on the hardest difficulty; enemies also have a limited number of arrows; not all soldiers have a firm will; side tasks are worth doing.
- Hardware requirements as stated by the reviewer: minimum CPU 233 MHz, 64 MB RAM, 4MB graphics; recommended CPU 500 MHz, 128 MB RAM, 8MB graphics.
